data.gender_notes: Ashique is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is passionate and devoted in love. The name Ashique carries the meaning “Lover, Beloved” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Urdu, Bengali. Parents who choose Ashique usually hope their child will grow to embody lover, beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ashique" holds a deep cultural resonance in the rich tapestry of Hindu traditions. It is a name that carries the essence of pure and unwavering love, parallel to the famous poetic phrases from the Indian subcontinent "Mohabbat ke taare seemsaab mein hai rehne wale, Dil ke neeche mausam dhokaane wale." (The stars of love are those who reside in the boundaries of the heart, and the weather that makes the heart flutter.)
data.spiritual_significance: Furthermore, Ashique holds significant spiritual significance in Hinduism. In the Bhagavad Gita's 10th chapter, Shree Krishna explains to Arjuna the importance of love for one's deity and the ultimate goal of reaching the divine. Ashique, as a name, represents this devotion and unwavering love towards the divine self or deity. The embodiment of this name inspires depth and compassion in one's spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashique: One deeply enamored with the Divine Beloved, devoted and yearning with an unwavering heart.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Mahabharata mentions a character named Ashique. The name Ashique carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In Hindu mythology, Ashique is associated with the god of love and desire.
